DEVOTION 1.0.4

First public build since 1.0.2. Combines the unreleased 1.0.3 with further
fixes. No new game required.

Thanks to DrHeisen, whose independent audit of 1.0.2 found a number of the
defects below.


=====================================================================
READ THIS IF YOU USE REQUIEM
=====================================================================

Devotion now ships its own copy of Scripts\TempleBlessingScript.pex.
Requiem's bugfix packs ship the same file, so in Mod Organizer 2 Devotion
must sit BELOW them (below = higher priority = wins the file). If Devotion
loads above them the shrine bug below comes back, and nothing will warn you.

To confirm: MO2 "Data" tab, find Scripts\TempleBlessingScript.pex, and it
should list Devotion as the provider.


=====================================================================
FIXED - SAVE DAMAGE
=====================================================================

* Runaway stat drift (save-corrupting). 418 of Devotion's 422 value-modifier
  effects were missing the engine's Recover flag, so every time a neglect,
  disfavor, pact-price or blessing effect switched on and off it baked the
  change in permanently. Stats drifted further every cycle for the life of
  the save - two users reported -22131% Magic Resistance and -5000 armour.
  All value-modifier effects now revert cleanly.

* Repairing an already-damaged save: use MCM > Devotion > Player >
  Maintenance > "Check stat damage" to see what your save is carrying, then
  "Repair stats" to clear it. Save first. Note that it also clears permanent
  modifiers other mods placed on those same values.

* Two observance effects still drifted, on a second effect type the first
  sweep missed.

* Devotion could stop working permanently after a single lost script tick.
  Dawn processing, pacts, the startup choice and the reconcile pass all
  stopped for the rest of the playthrough, with nothing in the log. A
  watchdog now restarts it on load.

* Uninstalling left effects on your character, including Malacath's speed
  price, so an uninstalled long-pact Orc stayed permanently slower.


=====================================================================
FIXED - SHRINES (REQUIEM USERS)
=====================================================================

* Praying wiped every buff you were carrying and gave nothing back.
  Requiem's bugfix packs add a line to the shrine script that dispels ALL
  your active magic effects - potions, fortify effects, enchantments,
  standing-stone powers. Normally that is invisible, because Requiem's
  blessing lands right afterwards. Devotion deliberately makes shrines grant
  no blessing (praying moves your standing with a god and writes a Book of
  Days entry; it is not meant to hand out stats from whatever overhaul you
  run), so in combination all that was left was the loss. Praying no longer
  dispels anything, and still awards piety.

* Not a Requiem user? You never had this. Base Skyrim's script does not
  dispel. The only change for you is that two vanilla pop-ups ("blessing
  removed" / "blessing received") no longer appear - both described
  something Devotion prevents anyway.


=====================================================================
FIXED - GODS REACTING CORRECTLY
=====================================================================

* Daedric pact prices and pool boons did nothing. Every pact's Health,
  Magicka and Stamina price and pool boon was authored so the game undid it
  instantly. They now correctly raise and lower your maximum pool, so pacts
  have the cost and benefit they describe.

* Hermaeus Mora's Champion boon was mis-wired - doubled Magicka and no
  Alteration. It now grants Alteration +20 and Fortify Magicka +20 as
  contracted.

* Disfavor stings and several neglect penalties were applying as bonuses.
  22 penalty effects were authored in a self-cancelling form the engine read
  as a buff. They now subtract as their descriptions say.

* Azura's likes and dislikes never loaded. An internal name mismatch meant
  twelve reaction rows and her whole per-race stance table were skipped, so
  she could not react to anything you did.

* Killing a Thalmor who attacked you counted as an unprovoked killing.

* A menu that could not open silently broke the Bosmer Old Contract - worst
  case, a forced reckoning severed the pact with no player input.


=====================================================================
ADDED
=====================================================================

* Bosmer Green Pact food. Eating meat now rewards a Wood Elf keeping the old
  pact - 22 vanilla and DLC meats (beef, goat, horse, venison, mammoth,
  horker, boar, ash hopper, chicken, rabbit and pheasant, raw and cooked).
  Eating plants remains the violation, unchanged. The existing daily limit
  applies, so it cannot be farmed.

* Requiem food support - Torn Flesh (called Strange Meat without Food and
  Beverages Redone), plus Requiem's skeever, fox, bear, mammoth, sabrecat
  and troll meat, and Wrothgar Tartare. Distributed by keyword, so it does
  nothing at all if you do not run Requiem.

* "Check stat damage" and "Repair stats" buttons - see above.


=====================================================================
IMPROVED
=====================================================================

* Equipping an item is dramatically cheaper. Devotion was re-reading and
  re-resolving its reaction data from scratch on every check, sixteen times
  per equip - in a large load order, hundreds of engine lookups every time
  you equipped anything. It is now resolved once when the save loads.

* Every scored action costs far less. Each god now knows in advance which
  events it can score, instead of all 34 paying for the lookup.

* Text formatting no longer runs 44 passes over every line of every toast,
  journal entry and panel string.

* No more Papyrus log line for every corpse.

* Larger, longer-lasting notifications on 1440p and 4K, and the toast box
  now sizes itself to the message instead of leaving dead space.

* Quieter background polling throughout.
